findings.note: TestNewlinePathCannotCollide cannot fail, and its premise is factually wrong. The comment says 'Two files whose naive concatenation would be identical' and the failure message says 'length-prefixed fields must make these preimages distinct', but SourceDiffHash's preimage is (path, hash) pairs where every hash is a fixed 16 hex characters, so path/field boundaries are never ambiguous there and no naive-concat collision is possible regardless of length prefixing. I verified this two ways: a standalone reimplementation with all length prefixes stripped still produces different digests for the two inputs (bd7e57c36a90f0eb vs c6e0816c67086d80), and stripping the length prefixes out of gitcontext.HashFields itself in a scratch copy leaves TestNewlinePathCannotCollide PASSING while TestSourceDiffHashFromDocumentedPreimage correctly fails. The test is also structurally incapable of exercising the production file-hash encoding: bf() feeds hashes computed by the test's own fileHashOf in as data. The property is genuinely pinned by TestSourceDiffHashFromDocumentedPreimage, so this is redundancy plus a misleading comment rather than a coverage hole; the encoding that actually needs the length prefix is the file-level (path, diff) preimage, where fileHash("ab","c") and fileHash("a","bc") collide without it.

evidence.note: 'Two files whose naive concatenation would be identical' — they are not, under SourceDiffHash's fixed-width-hash preimage

findings.note: TestSourceDiffHashIgnoresLocalChanges is a tautology against the current signature. PlanSourceHash is declared `func PlanSourceHash(_ Profile, files []gitcontext.BranchFile) string` (shards.go:82) — the Profile parameter is discarded at compile time — and the test calls it twice with the same `files` slice, so `PlanSourceHash(clean, files) != PlanSourceHash(dirty, files)` is a compile-time identity that no implementation of SourceDiffHash could make fail. The eight lines building the clean/dirty FileProfile fixture with SourceWorktree and SourceUntracked entries are dead weight that make the test read as if it were checking a filtering rule. Either assert the property where it is actually decidable (that the branch-files slice handed to PlanShards excludes local sources) or drop the fixture and keep the guarantee as the `_ Profile` signature plus a comment.

The name and the comment ('Close must not overwrite a more specific earlier failure') describe the Write-fails-and-Close-also-fails path, but the fixture passes `make(chan int)`, which fails inside json.Marshal at state.go:44 and returns before file.Write at state.go:48 is ever reached. findings.note: maxJSONLLineBytes is copied verbatim into four packages in this PR, with the same four-line rationale comment and the same `scanner.Buffer(make([]byte, 0, 64*1024), maxJSONLLineBytes+2)` incantation: internal/state:17, internal/findings:15, internal/reviewlog:17, internal/runchain:13. None existed at the base commit. These packages read files each other write (state.AppendJSONL is the writer for .metareview/runs.jsonl and findings.jsonl; the other three are readers), so the value is a cross-package interop invariant with no single definition and no test pinning the four equal — if one is ever lowered, the only symptom is 'bufio.Scanner: token too long'. The codebase already states the opposite discipline for exactly this kind of shared constant: gitcontext.HashFields is documented as 'the single definition of that encoding' precisely because a drifted second copy would be silent. Related asymmetry worth a line of thought while fixing: the constant is described as 'the JSONL line cap' but nothing enforces it on the write side, so state.AppendJSONL will happily write a row longer than 1 MiB that no reader can then parse, taking the whole file with it.

findings.note: Two small robustness gaps in the new jsonlStore, both on error paths. (1) TornFiles maps any os.ReadDir failure on the run directory to ERR_RUN_NOT_FOUND, so EACCES or ENOTDIR is reported to the operator as 'run not found' — every other reader in the file distinguishes IsNotExist from the rest (compare readRaw at store_jsonl.go:180-185, which reserves CodeRunNotFound for os.IsNotExist and routes everything else to pathErr). (2) Lock leaks the lock-file descriptor when syscall.Flock fails with anything other than EWOULDBLOCK: the EWOULDBLOCK arm closes f, but the generic `return nil, pathErr(0, err)` two lines later does not, and s.held was not populated so nothing else will close it. Both are cosmetic today (100% statement coverage in internal/fsm/run, and the flock arm is only reachable on EINTR/EBADF), but the first actively misleads and the second is a one-line fix.

evidence.note: TornFiles: any ReadDir error becomes CodeRunNotFound
readRaw shows the intended pattern: CodeRunNotFound only for os.IsNotExist
Lock returns without closing f when Flock fails with a non-EWOULDBLOCK error

findings.note: TestBitsBoundaryRecutsAll is weaker than its name and can silently vanish. The name promises the plan is re-cut in full, but the only assertion is `survived == len(after)` — it passes as soon as a single shard id changes, not when all do. It also opens with a t.Skip if the fixture stops crossing a bits boundary, so a later change to DefaultMaxBytesPerShard or to bucketBits could turn the test into a no-op that still reports success. Assert survived == 0 (which holds today: at bits=1 the ids are one hex digit and at bits=5 they are two, so no id can survive) and make the boundary condition a t.Fatal rather than a t.Skip.
